affected_predicate.description: All Download files whose names begin with bid_ are renamed in creation-date order to bid_{sequence_number}.{original_extension}.

competing_trace_defects.description: Before the reuse target, the agent repeatedly clicked the list/grid view toggle while describing it as a sort control; the display only alternated between list and grid without establishing the required creation-date sort.

chains.rationale: At reuse step 20, the inherited premise says the first file was renamed and treats the unsupported-image page as a failed second rename, even though no completed rename is visible. After returning to Downloads, bid_food_supplier_quote.txt remains visibly unchanged; the agent calls it the second file, selects it, and repeatedly attempts the overflow control while continuing to state that the first rename is complete. No rename dialog, new filename, or correction of the false completion premise appears through step 50, where the original bid_ filename remains selected. Thus the reused history visibly preserves false completion of the first rename, and the concrete renaming predicate remains unsatisfied in the observable trace.

summary: The sole strict-MHR chain visibly preserves an unsupported claim that an earlier rename was complete. That premise remains uncorrected while an original bid_ filename is selected and no rename operation becomes observable through the final trace step. An independent prefix defect repeatedly used the view-mode toggle as if it controlled sorting.
